chapter_theme: The rising of the true form (சொரூப உதயம்): the Lord pervades the elements so wholly that he cannot be marked off and circled, is beyond form and formlessness, and is reached only through the guru. Those who meditate on his form receive light; the poet sinks into the supreme light, crosses birth, and can say the First is the 'I'.
structure_note: The supreme guru in turiya and the Lord who pervades all (2835 to 2837); those beyond sect and the faults, and the soul and the Supreme (2838, 2839); form, formlessness and the guru (2840, 2841); the poet's own seeing (2842 to 2846). The grouping is mine; 2841 repeats உருவம் நினைப்பவர் in every line and 2842 பரஞ்சோதி.

2835.reading: The supreme guru, becoming the Supreme everywhere, joining everywhere firmly and without gap, the form that endures within the all-pervading form, stood having reached rare turiya.
2835.nuance: சொரூபம் (own form, true nature) is used twice: the guru's own form is said to endure within the form that pervades all. Whether the guru here is the Lord as guru or the human teacher become one with him is not fixed.

2836.reading: The water of the world in the surging sea, the tossing wind, fire and space: I do not know how to mark off the one who stretches long and wide through earth and sky and walk around him in worship.
2836.nuance: வலம்செய்தல் (circumambulation) needs a bounded object; the verse's point is that the Lord, spread through all five elements, cannot be bounded (வரைந்து) to be circled.

2837.reading: He stood there; the gods from Brahma and Mal on, and all who stand anywhere, praise him as Lord; our Lord, the sole master, abides, and swells forth as Lord of the worlds.
2837.nuance: The verbs run from standing there (அங்கு நின்றான்) to dwelling (தங்கி நின்றான்) to swelling forth (பொங்கி நின்றான்): the one Lord is both settled and overflowing.

2838.reading: Those who stand in clarity, without knowing even the trace of the sects in themselves, beyond the eight causes beginning with desire and the workings of darkness, become lords over the gods.
2838.nuance: காமாதி காரணம் எட்டும் (the eight beginning with desire) are traditionally the faults such as desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy, but the list of eight is not given. சுமையற்ற (burdenless) is unclear in its place. Sects (சமயம்) are again something to leave behind, as often in Tirumular.

2839.reading: One of the three kinds of gods is the first form and becomes different from it; so too the soul and the Supreme; that the far-off Siva may be gloriously reached in the three turiyas is the fitting path, say the books of the Lord.
2839.nuance: The analogy is compressed: as one god is both the source of the three gods and one of them, so the soul (அணு) and the Supreme are one and different. இறைநூல் (the Lord's books) is taken as the Agamas. The three turiyas are those of 'thou', 'that' and 'art' (2826).

2840.reading: Standing without form, he joins himself to forms; not being a womb, he himself becomes the womb; the wondrous Lord who stands without even formlessness cannot be reached by anyone without the guru.
2840.nuance: உரு, அரு (form, formless) and கரு (womb, embryo) rhyme through the verse. மாயப் பிரான் may be 'the wondrous Lord' or 'the Lord of maya'; Mal is also called மாயன், but here the subject is the one reached through the guru.

2841.reading: Those who think on his form find light rising within; those who think on his form see the aeons; those who think on his form become celestials; who in the world are equal to those who think on his form?
2841.nuance: The last line, உருவம் நினைப்பவர் உலகத்தில் யாரே, can mean 'who in the world is like them' or 'who in the world are such people' (they are rare). உருவம் may be the Lord's form or the guru's. After 2840 on the formless, the verse affirms meditation on form.

2842.reading: As I held to the Lord who is the supreme light, the supreme light sank into me; and as I sank and sank within the supreme light, I saw the supreme light declare itself.
2842.nuance: The movement is reciprocal: the light sinks into the poet, then the poet into the light. பறைய may be 'proclaim, speak' or 'wear away, vanish'; under the second reading the light itself fades from view in union.

2843.reading: As form, shape and quality swallow the ancient and become the rare water lily, so the guru of the true form, who weighs the four joined to him, truth and the rest, dwells in the dawning of bliss.
2843.nuance: The water lily image of the previous chapter (2827 to 2829). சுகோதயம் (the dawning of bliss) echoes the chapter title. தொல் விழுங்கி (swallowing the ancient) is obscure; it may refer to the old bonds.

2844.reading: In the true form of speechless bliss and silence, if one sees truth and the rest without bound, A merges and becomes U and M, and in the speechless letter it is the inner light.
2844.nuance: அகாரம், உகாரம், மகாரம் are the three parts of Om; உரையற்ற காரம் (the speechless letter) is taken as what lies beyond them, the point or nada. The verse ties the analysis of Om to the silence (மோனம்) of the true form.

2845.reading: The form known to the woman with breasts who did penance on the peak of the high mountain, I too, crossing vile and wicked birth, came to see in the thief who stands in the kalas.
2845.nuance: The woman doing penance on the mountain is taken as Uma, who won Siva by austerity on the Himalaya. கலைநின்ற கள்வன் (the thief who stands in the kalas) may be Siva hidden in the moon's digits, in the arts, or in the kalas of the yogic body; கள்வன் for the Lord who steals the heart is a devotional usage.

2846.reading: I came to know how the rare thing within comes about, how it leaves and that this is how it enters; there is no being misled and no other place now, and the First who is ourselves can be called 'I'.
2846.nuance: ஏமாப்பது இல்லை may mean 'there is no being deceived' or 'no other refuge is needed' (ஏமம், protection). The last line, நாமாம் முதல்வனும் நான் எனலாம், states the non-dual claim of 2820 in the poet's own voice.

links.note: 2820 says the Lord granted that 'I' and 'He' are not two and the poet's thinking ceased; 2846 speaks from the far side of that gift: the First can now be called 'I'.

2836 says the Lord stretches through water, wind, fire, space, earth and sky so that the poet cannot mark him off to walk around him (வரைந்து வலம்செயுமாறு அறியேனே); 2632 seeks him in the mountain, the sky, outside, the forge and the heart, and stands immersed (மூழ்கிநின்றேனே). Both start from the Lord everywhere: 2836 finds bounded worship impossible, 2632 finds the seeker immersed instead of circling.

1533 says those who saw the six sects did not see him, and tells the reader to be clear (தேறுமின் தெளிமின்) and enter without wavering. 2838 describes those who have done so: standing in clarity (தெளிவுடன் நின்றோர்) without even a trace of the sects (சமயச் சுவடும்) and beyond the eight causes from desire, they become lords of the gods.

2840 says the Lord, beyond form and formlessness, cannot be reached by anyone without the guru (குருவன்றி யாவர்க்கும் கூடஒண்ணாதே); 2559 describes those who cannot join the mark the guru set (கூடகில்லார் குரு வைத்த குறி) and wander making fine talk. The shared verb கூட shows 2559 as the consequence of 2840's rule.

Kural 3 says those who reach the feet of the one who walked on the flower will live long on earth (நிலமிசை நீடுவாழ்வார்); 2841 says those who think on his form see the aeons (ஊழியும் காண்பர்) and become celestials (உம்பரும் ஆவர்). Both promise lasting life to those who hold the Lord in mind; 2841 makes the means meditation on his form (உருவம் நினைப்பவர்).

141 says what one thinks on is Nandi's red holy form (சிந்திப்பது நந்தி செய்ய திருமேனி); 2841 repeats உருவம் நினைப்பவர் four times and gives the fruits: inner light, the aeons, celestial state. 141 states the practice as the guru's teaching; 2841 states what it yields.

2844 says that in the true form of speechless bliss and silence, A, U and M merge into the speechless letter (உரையற்ற காரத்தில்) and become inner light; 2496 says the three voids end in pure form where speech comes to its end (தூய சொரூபத்தில் சொல்முடிவாகுமே). Both place the true form where speech ends; 2844 reaches it through the letters of Om, 2496 through the three voids.

Near-repeat: 2845 and 2597 are the same verse (தலைநின்ற தாழ்வரை மீது தவஞ்செய்து முலைநின்ற மாதறி மூர்த்தியை ... கலைநின்ற கள்வன்), differing only in கள்வனில் and கள்வனை. The poet crossing vile birth and seeing the form the goddess knew through penance stands once under truthfulness (வாய்மை) and once under the rising of the true form.
